content.text:
Those pages are live. There is no `/jobs` index — each visa-sponsored role is its own URL. The directory is the sitemap.

**Open the list:** [https://kuchup.com/sitemap-jobs.xml](https://kuchup.com/sitemap-jobs.xml)

That XML has **57** open visa-sponsored positions. Each `<loc>` is a page you can open in the browser.

**Examples:**

- [https://kuchup.com/jobs/mollie-platform-engineer-ii-edge-and-network](https://kuchup.com/jobs/mollie-platform-engineer-ii-edge-and-network)
- [https://kuchup.com/jobs/dashlane-software-engineer-backend-node-js-aws](https://kuchup.com/jobs/dashlane-software-engineer-backend-node-js-aws)
- [https://kuchup.com/jobs/flixbus-senior-java-engineer-m-f-d-team-search-berlin-regular](https://kuchup.com/jobs/flixbus-senior-java-engineer-m-f-d-team-search-berlin-regular)
- [https://kuchup.com/jobs/n26-backend-engineer-lending](https://kuchup.com/jobs/n26-backend-engineer-lending)
- [https://kuchup.com/jobs/adyen-senior-software-engineer-financial-products](https://kuchup.com/jobs/adyen-senior-software-engineer-financial-products)

`https://kuchup.com/jobs/` itself 404s on purpose. Crawlers (and you) are supposed to go sitemap → slug page.

Those pages are what LinkedInBot is meant to crawl. They will not show on the Kuchup LinkedIn company page until LinkedIn actually indexes them — that is not instant. Until then, the sitemap and `/jobs/<slug>` URLs are the source of truth.
